steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Put potato pieces and water in a microwave-safe dish with a vented microwave-safe cover. Microwave on high for about 6–8 minutes in a roughly 1000 W microwave, until just fork-tender, then carefully uncover and drain. Prepare the rest during this step.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Before handling raw chicken, mix the oil, oregano, garlic, zest and pepper in a clean bowl. Give half to the drained potatoes, one quarter to beans and one quarter to chicken in separate bowls; give each one third of the salt. Spread potatoes over one half of a half-sheet pan, reserving the other half for beans. Set beans aside. Put unfolded chicken on the second pan. Keep the vegetable portion and tools away from raw-poultry juices.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Roast chicken and potatoes for 20–25 minutes. Add green beans to the vegetable pan after the first 10 minutes, keeping them in a separate area rather than piling them over potatoes. Swap racks at that addition. Chicken must reach 165°F; potatoes and beans should be tender. Remove each when ready.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Finish with lemon juice. Sprinkle yeast over vegetables after cooking.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Heat a mini waffle iron according to its manual; add an optional light coating of cooking spray.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Cook one mini chaffle at a time for about 2–3 minutes, until set and steam subsides. This four-portion batter makes four mini chaffles. Four sequential rounds take 8–12 minutes, plus about 5 minutes for heating and mixing. Adjust the round count when changing portions.

limitations: The original six portions mean six mini chaffles, rather than six complete adult meals. This four-portion batch makes four mini chaffles; nutrition is per chaffle.

The publisher’s 2–3-minute cooking time is per waffle-iron round. Six original rounds take 12–18 minutes of cooking, or 17–23 minutes with the publisher’s 5-minute preparation, before any additional preheating time.
Cook the four mini chaffles sequentially. The four-portion batch takes 13–17 minutes including preparation; waffle-iron behavior, preheating and larger batches may add time.

Ingredient quantities are scaled from 6 original portions to four portions. Fractions of whole items may need weighing or dividing after preparation. Larger batches need extra cooking space or batches; keep thickness and endpoint checks.
Adapted from Annie. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
At four portions, allow 8–12 minutes of sequential cooking plus the publisher’s 5-minute preparation. Follow the waffle-iron instructions and cook until set and steam subsides.

recipes.leftovers: Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.
recipes.safety: Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

recipes.title: Keto crack chicken (slow cooker)

prep: Use the publisher slow-cooker variation, not the insufficient-liquid pressure method.
Reserve cheddar, scallion and bacon for the finish; crisp bacon separately in a skillet.
Check poultry or reheated cooked chicken reaches 165°F at the thickest center.

rows.text: Fully thaw chicken. Put chicken and cream cheese in slow cooker.
Cover and cook LOW about 8 hours to 165°F; shred/return chicken, stir cheddar; top with stovetop-crisped bacon and scallion.
Whisk water, vinegar and all listed seasonings; pour over chicken.

steps.title: Load the slow cooker
steps.text: Use fully thawed chicken. Put it with cream cheese in the slow cooker. Whisk water, vinegar, chives, garlic powder, onion powder, chili flakes, dill, salt and pepper; pour over the chicken.

steps.title: Cook and shred
steps.text: Cover and cook on LOW for about 8 hours, following the cooker manual and confirming chicken reaches 165°F. Shred the cooked chicken with two forks and return it to the sauce; stir in cheddar.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Cook bacon in a stovetop skillet until crisp, drain and crumble. Scatter it and sliced scallion over the chicken. Allow preparation and finishing time in addition to the 8-hour slow cook.

tips: A 15-minute finishing allowance is a planning estimate; cooker behavior and chicken thickness decide the endpoint.
limitations: Uses Faith Gorsky’s published slow-cooker variation, under How to Make Crack Chicken in a Slow Cooker or Crock Pot at the original recipe link. Ingredient quantities are half the original eight-serving batch, giving four portions.

The publisher’s Instant Pot version uses ½ cup water for eight portions, or ¼ cup for four. This adaptation follows the publisher’s slow-cooker method; those small liquid amounts must not be assumed safe for pressure cooking.

Start with fully thawed chicken, follow your exact slow-cooker capacity and operating instructions, and verify 165°F. LOW cooking is approximately 8 hours; allow additional preparation and bacon-finishing time.

Nutrition retains the publisher’s estimate per original portion; proportional scaling preserves that portion. The publisher does not provide separate laboratory validation of the slow-cooker variation.
